disposition_reason: Cadmium, nickel and lead by MP-AES in 10 tomato pastes and 6 tomato ketchups (domestic and imported) bought in southwest Nigerian markets, with per-product means in Tables 2.1-2.3; arsenic and mercury below detection.

study.design: Market survey comparing domestic and imported tomato paste and ketchup, with health risk assessment
study.market: markets in Ijebu-Ode (Ogun), Lekki (Lagos), Ibadan (Oyo) and Idumota Market (Lagos)
study.method: 1 g digested in H2O2/HNO3 (3:1) at 70 °C for about 40 min; MP-AES (Agilent 4200); hydride generation for As and Hg
lod: Not given numerically; As and Hg 'below the LOD (0.00 mg.kg-1)'
study.qa: Five-level calibration 0.2-4.0 mg/L; no CRM or recovery reported

controls.outcome: Lead in tomato paste 0.128 vs 0.121 mg/kg; ketchup 0.136 vs 0.102 mg/kg; cadmium paste 0.078 vs 0.088, ketchup 0.083 vs 0.075 mg/kg; differences not significant (p>0.05)

unresolved: Nickel unit scale conflicts between Table 2.2 header (x 10-3), the text (10-4 mg/kg) and the abstract (about 0.3 mg/kg); nickel value_ugkg left null.
Text says cadmium exceeded the USEPA 0.010 mg/kg limit in only 10% of pastes and 6.25% of samples, but every printed cadmium value (0.066-0.107 mg/kg) exceeds 0.010 mg/kg.
Number of replicates per product and purchase dates not stated; 'Source: Laboratory, 2023' is the analysis attribution, not a collection date.
Table 2.5 ketchup lead DIR (8.69 x 10-4) is about ten times the paste value despite similar concentrations; not reconciled.
Proxy only for the barbecue-sauce, canned-spaghetti, pasta-sauce and tomato-soup pages: none of those foods was measured.

regulatory_or_exposure.value: Cd: USEPA 0.010 mg/kg, EC 0.05 mg/kg; Pb: WHO/EC 0.10 mg/kg; Ni: WHO 5 x 10-3 mg/kg
